About Gringo's Washboard Band

After more than a decade playing across South America and Europe, Gringo's Washboard Band is back with the show Root of the Oppressed, at a time that needs music more than ever.

“Root of the Oppressed is a history lesson turned into music.”

Led by Brazilian percussionist Guto Krainski, Gringo's Washboard Band has been telling the story of African American music.

Gringo's Washboard Band has played many blues and jazz festivals in Europe and South America, including Santa Maria Blues Festival, Mississippi Delta Blues Festival, Jazz Mansion and Ilha Comprida Festival Internacional, among many others. The band has also stood out on TV shows such as Rede Globo's SuperStar and Got Talent Portugal (where it reached the semi-finals in 2026), and won the Portugal Blues Challenge.

The show Root of the Oppressed offers an immersion in the neglected narratives of African American music. Far from commercial clichés, the concert brings to light the harshness of racial segregation, misogyny and slavery-like labour — historical realities that still echo in today's society.

Gringo's Washboard Band

Founded in 2013 by Guto Krainski (percussionist and storyteller), Gringo's Washboard Band brings together traditional jazz musicians. Its music draws on the blues, the revolution of Ida Cox and the spirit of New Orleans — all revitalised for a contemporary audience that, it seems, was waiting for exactly that.
